thought_title: Delayed reply because of disasters; praise of Corinth's former virtue
orientation: The Roman church is writing to the Corinthian church, explaining why their reply has been slow and then praising the Corinthians' former good conduct before rebuking their present faction.
pass_a_gloss: Because of the sudden and successive misfortunes and calamities that happened to us, we think we have made a slower response concerning the matters being sought among you, beloved, namely the alien and foreign to the elect of God, defiled and unholy faction, which a few individuals, being rash and self-willed, kindled to such a degree of folly that your reverend and famous and to all people lovable name was greatly blasphemed. For who, having sojourned among you, did not approve your all-virtuous and firm faith? And did not marvel at your prudent and gentle piety in Christ? And did not proclaim the magnificent character of your hospitality? And did not bless your perfect and secure knowledge? For you did all things without partiality and walked in the ordinances of God, submitting to your leaders, and giving the fitting honor to the elders among you: and you instructed the young to think moderate and reverend things: and you commanded the women to accomplish all things in blameless and reverend and pure conscience, loving their own husbands as is fitting: and being in the rule of submission you taught them to manage the things of the house reverently, being very prudent.

lemmas.gloss: having sojourned, having visited as a stranger

choices.why: Glossary term; the divisive uprising in Corinth, rendered as 'faction' per the fixed glossary.
Glossary term; the duly appointed leaders of the Corinthian church, rendered as 'elders' per the fixed glossary.
Glossary term; God's chosen people, rendered as 'the elect' per the fixed glossary.
Glossary term; the few persons who stirred up the faction, rendered as 'individuals' per the fixed glossary.
Glossary term; obedience to rightful order, rendered as 'submission' per the fixed glossary.
Here means attention or reply to the matters raised, not 'conversion'; 'response' fits the epistolary context of answering inquiries.

pass_b_english: Because sudden and repeated misfortunes and calamities have fallen upon us, we think we have been slow to respond to the matters you have asked about, beloved. We mean that defiled and unholy faction, alien and foreign to the elect of God, which a few rash and arrogant individuals have kindled to such a pitch of folly that your revered name, famous and worthy of love among all people, has been greatly blasphemed.

For who has ever visited you and not approved your all-virtuous and firm faith? Who has not admired your sober and gentle piety in Christ? Who has not proclaimed the magnificent character of your hospitality? Who has not called your perfect and secure knowledge blessed?

For you did everything without partiality and walked in the ordinances of God. You submitted to your leaders and gave due honor to the elders among you. You instructed the young to think moderate and reverent thoughts. You directed the women to accomplish everything with a blameless, reverent, and pure conscience, loving their husbands as is fitting. You taught them to manage their household affairs with reverence, remaining within the proper order of submission, exercising complete self-control.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by naming the faction as the subject of the response, broke the long first paragraph into two sentences, and divided the dense final paragraph into shorter sentences with clearer subjects and verbs.

Clarified 'the elect of God' as a consistent reference, kept 'elders' as the office term, and smoothed 'rule of submission' to 'proper order of submission' while preserving every claim and qualification.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'the elect of God' is real: the source has τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ θεοῦ, and the glossary entry for ἐκλεκτοί specifies 'the elect' as the English rendering. Changed to 'the elect'.
The glossary issue about 'leaders' is not a mistranslation: the source has τοῖς ἡγουμένοις, which is a different term from πρεσβύτεροι/ἐπίσκοποι and is correctly rendered 'leaders'. No change needed.

The mistranslation issue about 'rule of submission' is real: the source has τῷ κανόνι τῆς ὑποταγῆς, and the glossary entry for κανών specifies 'rule' as the English rendering, but 'order of submission' is more natural and accurate here. Changed to 'order of submission'.

last_rejected.why: Not in glossary, but 'elders' is fixed for πρεσβυτέροις; however ἡγουμένοις is distinct. No glossary violation.
last_rejected.ruling: ἡγουμένους means leaders; rendering within normal range. No glossary violation claimed.

last_rejected.quote: remaining within the rule of submission
last_rejected.source_quote: ἔν τε τῷ κανόνι τῆς ὑποταγῆς ὑπαρχούσας
last_rejected.why: Source says women are 'in the rule of submission,' not 'remaining within' it; but sense is close. More critically: 'exercising complete self-control' applies to women (πάνυ σωφρονούσας), but 'remaining within the rule of submission' is misattributed—it's the women who are in the rule, not the household management that remains within it.
last_rejected.fix: You taught them, being in the rule of submission, to manage their households with reverence, exercising complete self-control.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπαρχούσας grammatically modifies γυναιξίν; English correctly attributes 'rule of submission' to women. Sense preserved.

last_rejected.quote: the matters you have asked about
last_rejected.why: Dative παρ’ ὑμῖν marks disputes among the Corinthians, not a request they sent to Rome.
last_rejected.fix: the matters in dispute among you
last_rejected.ruling: τῶν ἐπιζητουμένων παρ' ὑμῖν πραγμάτων is ambiguous: 'matters sought/inquired about by you'. Many standard translations (Lake, Lightfoot) render it 'asked about', so this is within normal range.
